methodology_notes: New comparison: no other E11x benchmark tests a batch of MIXED protein lengths -- every prior benchmark uses one fixed length per call, at exact bucket boundaries (zero padding waste by construction).

jax_bucket_pad_tile groups structures by xtrax.tiling.select_bucket assignment (the same E4.5-confirmed {64,128,256,512} boundaries), pads each group to its bucket size, one jax.vmap'd energy call per group -- this is what aminx's own bucket+pad+tile composition does.
pytorch_pad_to_batch_max pads every structure to the single largest length in the WHOLE batch (no bucketing concept) -- the naive dynamic-batching approach a PyTorch user would reach for first.

pytorch_per_structure_loop has zero padding waste by construction (one call per structure at its native length) but zero batching benefit either -- closest to what score_decoys.py itself actually does (one native length at a time, never mixed).
No SM120 XLA autotuning workaround applied here -- CPU-only local run. A cluster (GPU) run MUST set XLA_FLAGS=--xla_gpu_shard_autotuning=false per ~/.claude/rules/CLUSTER.md.
A row with 'error' instead of 'wall_clock_mean_ms' means that strategy raised during timing -- the other strategies in this file completed normally and are unaffected.
